title: Breast pain
claims: Breast pain is usually linked to periods and usually begins up to 2 weeks before a period, gets worse and then goes away when the period ends; it feels dull, heavy or aching and affects both breasts, sometimes spreading to the armpit.

Other causes include injuries or sprains to the neck, shoulder or back, medicines such as the contraceptive pill and some antidepressants, conditions such as mastitis or a breast abscess, pregnancy, and hormone changes during menopause.
Breast pain by itself is unlikely to be a symptom of cancer.
The NHS suggests wearing a properly fitted bra during the day and a soft bra to sleep in, and states there is little evidence that vitamin E tablets or evening primrose oil help with breast pain.
The NHS advises seeing a GP if breast pain is not improving or painkillers are not helping, if there is a family history of breast cancer, or if there are signs of pregnancy.
The NHS advises an urgent GP appointment or NHS 111 if breast pain occurs with a very high temperature or feeling hot and shivery, or if any part of the breast is red, hot or swollen.

The NHS lists urgent review for a hard lump that does not move around, nipple discharge that may be streaked with blood, a change in breast shape, skin dimpling like orange peel, or a rash on or around the nipple or a nipple that has sunk into the breast.
